interpretation: These are saved endpoint extrema from the common velocity U and shared T fields. Gas Mach uses common U divided by ideal-air sound speed at this T; it is not a measured relative gas velocity.

The high-speed point is gas-dominant and lies just downstream of the recorded internal nozzle plane. Its local Courant number is approximately the configured 0.5 maximum, so the endpoint evidence is consistent with the near-lip gas jet controlling the shrinking time step. This endpoint alone does not prove a causal time-history.

The peak-speed cell's kinetic-energy scale is much larger than its local Cp*T scale; a bulk-tank-to-cell isentropic comparison is also recorded as a screening inconsistency. Neither is a complete gas energy balance or a strict physical bound: this shared-T case has no separately conservative air-temperature field, and interface, wall, pressure-work, model, and numerical energy transfer terms are not resolved here.

The 5 kPa and 10 kPa replay arms show almost identical extreme U/T/Co values, so this peak behavior is not materially changed by the tested pMin reduction over the replay window. The near-identical bulk outputs do not clear these local extremes or establish physical validation.
No cavitation conclusion is made. The audited extreme cells are gas-dominant at the saved endpoint, and the earlier intermediate clamp-cell alpha/T/location trace is unavailable.
